outcomes.text: Discuss how the family is changing in Spanish-speaking countries.
Give views on attitudes to marriage and divorce.
Explain the influence of the Catholic Church on society.
Discuss the influence of the internet on Hispanic society.
Weigh the benefits and dangers of social networks.
Talk about the role of smartphones in society.
Describe women's place in the job market.
Discuss machismo and feminism.
Discuss the rights of gay and transgender people.

topics.title: 3.2.1 Artistic culture in the Hispanic world

outcomes.text: Discuss the influence of singers and musicians.
Discuss the influence of television and film stars.
Discuss the influence of models.
Describe regional traditions and customs in Spain.
Describe regional food and gastronomy.
Discuss the regional languages of Spain.
Describe heritage sites and pre-Hispanic civilisations such as Machu Picchu and the Alhambra.
Discuss art and architecture.
Discuss musical heritage and its diversity.
Use the grammatical system of Spanish actively and accurately, building on GCSE grammar.
Use noun gender and singular and plural forms, including male/female pairs; recognise affective suffixes.
Use definite and indefinite articles, el before stressed-a feminine nouns, and lo plus adjective.
Make adjectives agree and place them correctly, including apocopation.
Form comparatives and superlatives and use adjectives as nouns.
Use demonstrative, indefinite, possessive, interrogative and exclamatory adjectives; recognise cuyo.
Use cardinal and ordinal numbers, number agreement, and expressions of time and date.
Form -mente adverbs and adverb comparatives, use adjectives as adverbs, and use interrogative adverbs.
Use quantifiers and intensifiers such as muy, bastante, poco, mucho.
Use subject, object, reflexive and stressed pronouns, with correct position and order, including se for le(s).
Use relative, demonstrative, indefinite, possessive and interrogative pronouns, and show possession with indirect objects.
Conjugate regular, irregular, radical- and orthographic-changing verbs in all tenses and moods, and make verbs agree with subjects.
Use present, preterite, imperfect, future, conditional, perfect, future perfect, conditional perfect and pluperfect.
Use the infinitive, gerund and past participle, and hay que in all tenses.
Use verbal paraphrases such as ir a, estar plus gerund, acabar de, estar para and llevar plus gerund.
Use the subjunctive in commands, conditional sentences, after conjunctions of time and after para que and sin que.
Recognise the subjunctive in relative clauses, other conjunctions, and verbs of wishing, doubt and emotion; follow sequence of tenses.
Express the passive and impersonal subject with reflexives, ser or estar plus past participle, and nuance reflexive verbs.
Choose between tú, usted and vos; use verbs followed by infinitive, preposition, gerund or perception; use ser and estar.
Use simple and complex prepositions, personal a, and distinguish por from para.
Use coordinating and subordinating conjunctions of cause, purpose, proviso, supposition, time and concession; recognise que introducing a clause.
Form negative sentences.
Form questions.
Form commands.
Use word order, including subject after verb; recognise focalisation.
Use hace/desde hace time expressions, cleft sentences and comparative constructions.
Report speech using indirect speech.
Use discourse markers such as es que, por ejemplo, ahora bien.
Use fillers such as pues and bueno in speech.
Weigh the benefits and drawbacks of immigration.
Describe immigration within the Hispanic world.
Explain the problems faced by undocumented migrants.
Discuss racist and xenophobic attitudes.
Describe measures taken against racism.
Explain anti-racist legislation.
Discuss how different cultures live together.
Discuss the role of education in integration.
Discuss the role of religions in integration.

topics.title: 3.2.2 Aspects of political life in the Hispanic world

outcomes.text: Discuss whether young people are politically active or apathetic.
Discuss youth unemployment.
Describe young people's ideal society.
Describe Franco's dictatorship.
Trace how the Spanish monarchy has evolved.
Describe Latin American dictators.
Judge how effective demonstrations and strikes are.
Explain the power of trade unions.
Describe examples of social protest such as the 15-M and the Madres de la Plaza de Mayo.
Study all A-level extra grammar in addition to the AS list.
Use the relative adjective cuyo.
Use the subjunctive in relative clauses, after other subordinating conjunctions, and with verbs of wishing, doubt, emotion and possibility.
Use que to introduce a clause.
Use comparative constructions such as más de lo que, and recognise concession with por muy... que.
Study either one text and one film, or two texts, and respond critically in Spanish.
Analyse the concepts, issues, form and technique of a work, such as narrative voice or camera work.

Study García Márquez's Crónica de una muerte anunciada.
Study Esquivel's Como agua para chocolate.

Study Ruiz Zafón's La sombra del viento.
Study Allende's La casa de los espíritus.
Study Bécquer's Rimas.

Study Castresana's El otro árbol de Guernica.
Study García Márquez's El coronel no tiene quien le escriba.
Study the film El laberinto del fauno.
Study the film Ocho apellidos vascos.
Study the film María, llena eres de gracia.
Study the film Volver.
Study the film Abel.
